summary: When a tenant network spans EVPN and IPVPN domains, the BGP domains must interwork for end-to-end connectivity. This Standards Track document defines the interworking procedures.

eli5.summary: Two cities use different road systems, and this gives rules for linking them so travelers can cross smoothly.

questions: how to interconnect evpn and ipvpn
subtitle: How EVPN and IPVPN networks of the same tenant exchange routes, plus a Domain Path attribute that stops loops.

tldr.problem: A tenant network can span domains that use EVPN and domains that use IPVPN for inter-subnet forwarding. Joining them needs clear rules for route selection, attribute handling and loop prevention, and redundant gateways can otherwise redistribute a route in a circle.
tldr.mechanism: Interworking PEs (composite and gateway) re-originate routes between domains. A new optional transitive BGP attribute, D-PATH, lists the domains a route has crossed so that a gateway can spot its own domain and flag the route as looped. Route selection prefers the shortest D-PATH.
tldr.outcome: Tenants can have end-to-end connectivity across mixed EVPN and IPVPN domains with loop protection. D-PATH is off by default and must be enabled by configuration on the gateway PEs.

today: RFC 10039 is a Proposed Standard published in September 2026. It has not been obsoleted or updated by another RFC, and IANA has assigned BGP Path Attribute code 36 to D-PATH.

sections.title: The Problem and the Approach
sections.content:
EVPN is a unified BGP control plane for both intra- and inter-subnet forwarding (ISF) in tenant networks. Some parts of a tenant network use EVPN, while others use the BGP VPN-IPv4 and VPN-IPv6 address families (IPVPN). RFC 10039 defines how these domains interwork, including the interconnection of two EVPN domains, two IPVPN domains, or one of each.

The IP prefixes in EVPN Route Type 2 (RFC 9135) and Route Type 5 (RFC 9136) are re-originated into other address families such as IPVPN, and the other way round. An Interworking PE imports routes from one domain, installs them in an IP-VRF, and re-originates them with encapsulation suited to the next domain. This makes the solution independent of each domain's transport encapsulation.

The danger is a control plane loop. If gateway PE1 turns an IPVPN route into an EVPN IP Prefix route and gateway PE2 re-advertises that route back into the IPVPN domain, a loop may form. The new Domain Path (D-PATH) attribute is designed to prevent this. Because it changes best-path selection for IPVPN and EVPN, the document updates the procedures of RFC 4271 for those families, but only when D-PATH is used.
sections.eli5: When a letter passes between two post offices that work differently, it can get passed back and forth forever. This document sets rules so that never happens.

sections.title: Domains and Interworking PEs
sections.content:
A domain is a set of PEs of the same tenant whose packets need no tenant IP lookup at any transit router. Domain boundaries are not limited to an Autonomous System or an IGP instance. A regular domain uses a single ISF SAFI (IPVPN or EVPN). A composite domain uses both.

An Interworking PE keeps one IP-VRF per tenant and can advertise a prefix as an EVPN or IPVPN route. It comes in two kinds:

  • A composite PE advertises a prefix as an IPVPN route to IPVPN peers, as an EVPN route to EVPN peers, and as both to a Route Reflector.
  • A gateway PE connects two or more distinct domains and either re-originates routes with the same SAFI or translates between SAFIs.

A single PE can do both jobs for the same tenant. The term ISF SAFI means SAFI 128 (IPVPN) or SAFI 70 (EVPN), and the procedures apply only to these two.
sections.eli5: A composite station speaks both road languages at once. A gateway station sits on the border and passes things between two separate countries.

sections.title: The D-PATH Attribute
sections.content:
D-PATH is an optional, transitive BGP Path Attribute. Like AS_PATH it is a sequence of domain segments. Each segment has a 1-octet length (the number of domains) followed by the domains. Each domain is written <DOMAIN-ID:ISF_SAFI_TYPE>.

The DOMAIN-ID is 6 octets: a 4-octet Global Administrator and a 2-octet Local Administrator. All gateway PEs attached to the same domain MUST use the same DOMAIN-ID, and a gateway between two domains uses two different ones. The ISF_SAFI_TYPE is a 1-octet informational field recording the SAFI in which the gateway received the route. It does not affect loop detection or path selection.

When a gateway re-originates a route, it MUST prepend the domain it learned the route from. The leftmost entry is the most recent domain. The rightmost is the Domain of Origin. A route with no D-PATH yet gets a new one with a single entry. D-PATH MUST be explicitly enabled by configuration and MUST NOT go with routes other than IPVPN and EVPN.

For loop detection, a received route is flagged looped if its D-PATH contains any DOMAIN-ID configured locally on the IP-VRF, whatever the ISF_SAFI_TYPE. A looped route MUST NOT be exported to any other domain, and it is installed only if it is the best path. For a gateway's own local routes, the RECOMMENDED choice is to advertise with a D-PATH holding a locally configured DOMAIN-ID and ISF_SAFI_TYPE 0.
sections.eli5: Each border station stamps the route's passport with the country it came from. If a station sees a stamp from its own country, it knows the route has gone in a circle and stops it.

sections.title: Attribute Propagation Modes
sections.content:
When a gateway re-advertises a route into another domain, there are two modes for the other BGP Path Attributes.

In No Propagation Mode, the default, the gateway re-initializes the attributes as if the prefix were locally originated. D-PATH is not propagated, so redundant gateways may be susceptible to loops. Policies or the Route Origin extended community can reduce this, but they do not guarantee prevention.

In Uniform Propagation Mode, the gateway keeps a limited set of attributes by default: AS_PATH, D-PATH (for IPVPN and EVPN routes only), the IBGP-only attributes LOCAL_PREF, ORIGINATOR_ID and CLUSTER_ID, MED, AIGP, and the community attributes. Other attributes SHOULD NOT be propagated unless policy allows it. Encapsulation Extended Communities, Route Target Extended Communities and EVPN-specific Extended Communities SHOULD NOT be copied, because they could cause a receiving PE to misread a route. Only the best path's attributes are propagated.

A gateway MAY also aggregate many host routes into one aggregate route. An aggregate SHOULD NOT be advertised unless all contributing routes have the same D-PATH DOMAIN-ID members.
sections.eli5: When a parcel crosses the border, the station can either throw away the old labels and start fresh, or copy over a short list of safe ones. Risky labels are never copied.

sections.title: Choosing the Best Route
sections.content:
A PE may hear the same prefix from several ISF SAFIs. Standard BGP best-path selection first yields a set of best EVPN paths and a set of best non-EVPN paths. When both sets are non-empty, the PE MUST run a tie-break on their union. It follows RFC 4271 with these additions:

  1. Right after the Local Preference step, remove routes that do not have the shortest D-PATH. A route without D-PATH counts as length zero.
  2. The standard steps then continue in order.
  3. If any remaining route is an EVPN MAC/IP Advertisement route (Route Type 2), remove all EVPN IP Prefix routes (Route Type 5).
  4. If ECMP is enabled and both EVPN and non-EVPN paths remain, keep both. Otherwise the EVPN path MUST be selected.

In one of the RFC's examples, an EVPN route with D-PATH length 1 beats an IPVPN route with D-PATH length 2, even though the IPVPN route has a shorter AS_PATH.
sections.eli5: If two paths lead to the same place, pick the one that crossed the fewest borders. If it is still a tie, pick the more detailed kind of route.

sections.title: Composite and Gateway PE Behavior
sections.content:
Composite PEs. They MUST advertise the same prefixes using each ISF SAFI to the Route Reflector. If the attributes match, the receiving composite PE picks the EVPN route over the IPVPN route. The Route Reflector sends EVPN routes only to peers with EVPN enabled. Plain IPVPN PEs only see IPVPN routes, so EVPN's advanced forwarding features are not available to them.

Gateway PEs. A gateway MUST export a prefix learned in SAFI x to SAFI y if the route is installed in the IP-VRF as the best valid route, an active session for SAFI y exists, and export policy allows it. It MUST NOT export a malformed route or a looped route. In Uniform Propagation Mode it MUST add or extend D-PATH. It uses the IP-VRF's RD, and label allocation is a local matter. It MUST support different Route Target sets per domain on the same IP-VRF.

An informative note warns that a route which crosses a non-EVPN domain loses EVPN-specific attributes. For example, a non-zero ESI is reset to zero.
sections.eli5: Border stations only pass along good, non-circular routes. Some special features of one road system get lost when a route crosses through the other.

sections.title: Error Handling
sections.content:
A D-PATH is malformed if a domain segment has length zero or runs past the end of the attribute, if fewer than 8 octets remain after the last parsed segment, or if the whole attribute is under 8 octets. Each domain is encoded in 7 octets, so a segment takes 1 plus 7 times the number of domains. A BGP speaker receiving a malformed D-PATH SHALL apply the treat-as-withdraw procedure of RFC 7606.

Unrecognized ISF_SAFI_TYPE values MAY be accepted and are not an error. If D-PATH appears more than once, all instances after the first MUST be discarded. D-PATH on any AFI/SAFI other than IPVPN or EVPN also gets treat-as-withdraw.

If a gateway wrongly propagates attributes, such as an Encapsulation Extended Community, a receiving PE follows RFC 8365 for multiple encapsulations. A receiving IPVPN PE MUST ignore EVPN Extended Communities.
sections.eli5: If a passport stamp is torn or makes no sense, the receiving station ignores the whole route instead of guessing.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The security considerations of RFC 9136, RFC 8365 and RFC 4364 apply. Wrong DOMAIN-ID values, or gateways that do not all support D-PATH, can cause false-positive loop detection, discarded traffic, or inconsistent routing. Since D-PATH is transitive, a malicious actor could inject false domain information.

To limit this, D-PATH is restricted to IPVPN and EVPN routes inside "walled garden" VPNs. A conforming PE MUST remove D-PATH before advertising a prefix to a CE in a SAFI 1 route. Upgraded PEs SHOULD discard IPVPN or EVPN routes carrying D-PATH from non-upgraded peers.

Uniform Propagation Mode lets an attacker try to inject attributes that influence path selection in remote domains. Operators may choose No Propagation Mode to avoid that, at the cost of downstream PEs no longer seeing the original attributes.
sections.eli5: The passport stamps only work inside a trusted group of countries. Stamps must never leak onto the public roads, and a station may skip copying labels if it does not trust them.
